Need feedback on a Game Censorship IMDB/Mrskin;)

So, there I was, googling about yet another game to dig up the state of censorship before buying it, but an annoyance has been creeping up for a while now. That is, every time I google information, I get led to editorial sites and articles about the game, within which I have to read up the information. While I do like the editorial format to keep up to date, it is not a good format if you want a quick reference.

And that's basically what I have been tinkering with since this week. A website that is data-driven and lists information about censorship in a raw data style instead of an editorial style.

Now that I have it set up in a presentable state, I thought I might get some feedback to get some ideas from other people. Here's a link to the "Tokyo Mirage" entry. While the information on there is largely correct (I hope), it's not what is relevant to me. Rather, I want to know about the look & feel of it or even suggestions. There are things that are missing that are already planned (like site navigation) but I think that's a given. I just don't have other pages to link to yet :P. With that said, here are the other points I need feedback on.

  1. Are you interested in such a website to start with?

When I started this, I did so under the impression that people other people might also be interested in it. However, I could be wrong on this and so I just felt like asking before committing more of my time into this. After all, I will have to rely on a bit of crowd sourcing to have enough information to actually be relevant in the grand scheme of things. That said, would you be interested to post the occasional suggestion or resource (like image to go along with text) as anon i.e. no login required?

  1. What do you consider censorship?

This seems like an odd question at first but if you start going down the rabbit hole, there are quite a few nuances that make it difficult to answer. For my purpose and the purpose of the site, I define censorship as something that was stripped from a supposed "complete version". That is, if a version of a game lacks content that the same game has in the region of origin, then it is censored. This seems to be a good definition until you get to cases like R. Mika's butt slap however. As far as I know, the butt slap was 'removed' during production and is not included in any version of Street Fighter 5. Even though I personally think that this is censorship, I would not be considered censorship according to the previous definition. So why am I making a big deal out of it and not just add it anyway? Consider Senran Kagura: Estival Versus. That game has lots of intentional censorship. However, how do you objectively distinguish between Senran Kagura's censorship and SF5's censorship? R. Mika's buttslap was intentionally removed by devs from all version of the game. The same can be said for Senran Kagura. This isn't a case of me not considering R. Mika's buttslap to not be censorship but rather, I don't know how I can objectively rationalize it without opening a can of worms where I would technically have to include things that were never meant to be there.

The reason I want to keep the rules of "what to include" in the database as objective and rational as possible is to avoid disagreements and be as consistent as possible. That's the reason I want to go with the practical approach of listing stuff that you can get an uncensored version of without resorting to mods. How do you see it?

  1. How would I deal with images in an ethical way?

If you watch the entry for Tokyo Mirage, you will see a few real images along with some placeholder ones that I used to test some design features. While I fully admit to shamelessly stealing these images off google to set up the page, I am aware that this is not the proper way to do things if I'm going to roll the site out for serious.

What I plan to do is to use the Mantis bug tracker software, usually used to track bugs found by anon people, in order to track suggestions. People would then also link to pictures that they think would fit into a censorship entry. My hope is that people will post images they made themselves or at least get permission to use them. But even so, I know that not everybody works like that so are there things I can do to avoid anything unethical related to usage of pictures?

  1. Cut to the chase, how much Patreon-shekels will this take to fund?

Actually, what you are seeing is the real thing already. It is not a mock-up. I am using a proprietary CMS that allows me to severely cut down any development costs (time investment included) and I set up the current state of the site within 10h or so. As you can see, there is also no ads and no tracking cookies. For now, hosting is covered without me having to pay anything. Evidently, this may not always stay that way if the site should take off because "traffic be expensive yo" but for now, that's the state of affairs and it should run like that for a while.

*actual dev is Sulfura
